critical_code_review_comments: FIXED by testing agent in /app/backend/routes_messaging.py: PATCH /api/tickets/{ticket_id} had `update.setdefault('$push', {})` which polluted the dict that was later passed to `{'$set': update}`. MongoDB correctly rejected with 'The dollar ($) prefixed field $push in $push is not allowed' (code 52). Removed the stray setdefault line — separate update_one calls now do (a) $push to thread, then (b) $set on plain fields. Verified by test_ticket_creation_and_notifications_flow.

notifications query uses $or with [{user_id}, {role}, {role:'*'}] + institution_id scope — correct multi-recipient model. Note: for super_admin the institution_id filter will only return notifications where institution_id matches super_admin's own institution_id (null), so super_admin currently cannot see cross-tenant notifications via this endpoint. Not blocking; flag if cross-tenant inbox is desired.

Role-broadcast notification creation in tickets POST writes user_id=None + role='registrar'/'institution_admin'. mark_read endpoint filter uses `$or:[{user_id:user.id},{role:user.role},{role:'*'}]` without institution_id — a registrar in tenant A could in theory mark-read a registrar-broadcast notification belonging to tenant B (since role matches). Low-risk because list endpoint already scopes by institution_id, but for defense-in-depth add institution_id to the mark_read filter too.

rca of the issue: PATCH /api/tickets/{ticket_id} 500 — pymongo.errors.WriteError code 52. Root cause: line 199 in routes_messaging.py had `update.setdefault('$push', {})` immediately before doing a separate $push update; this mutation left a literal '$push' key inside `update`, which was then sent as `db.support_tickets.update_one({'id': ticket_id}, {'$set': update})`. MongoDB forbids $-prefixed field names inside a $set replacement document. Reproduction: POST /api/tickets as student → PATCH that ticket as registrar with `{'status':'resolved','reply':'Handled'}`. Mitigation applied: removed the stray setdefault line so the function performs (a) $push on thread when reply is given, then (b) $set on the remaining whitelisted fields. Verified green via test_ticket_creation_and_notifications_flow.
